note: Literature confirms NFU1 mutations cause a spectrum from classic infantile MMDS1 with severe cavitating leukoencephalopathy to milder, late-onset spastic paraplegia phenotypes with slowly progressive leukoencephalopathy.

evidence.text: NFU1 mutations can present with a milder phenotype characterized by later onset, slowly progressive spastic paraparesis with relapsing-remitting episodes, long survival, and slowly evolving leukoencephalopathy rather than lethal infantile neurodegeneration.

source.title: New spastic paraplegia phenotype associated to mutation of NFU1
source.quote: We report a new NFU1 mutated patient presenting with a milder phenotype characterized by a later onset, a slowly progressive spastic paraparesis with relapsing-remitting episodes, mild cognitive impairment and a long survival... Our case clearly suggests the importance of considering NFU1 mutation in slowly evolving leukoencephalopathy with high glycine concentration.

evidence.text: Early-onset NFU1-related multiple mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome type 1 prominently features diffuse and symmetric cavitating cystic leukoencephalopathy with severe developmental regression.

source.title: NFU1-related disorders as key differential diagnosis of cavitating leukoencephalopathy
source.quote: Neuroimaging showed diffuse and symmetric cavitating cystic leukoencephalopathy. Whole-exome sequencing revealed compound heterozygous mutations in the NFU1 gene, providing definite genetic diagnosis of multiple mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome type 1. We report a rare presentation of early-onset cystic leukoencephalopathy in the context of multiple mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome type 1.
